sanskrit: catvāry āhuḥ sahasrāṇi varṣāṇāṃ tat kṛtaṃ yugam tasya tāvac chatī saṃdhyā saṃdhyāṃśaś ca tathāvidhaḥ
english: They say the Kṛta age numbers four thousand years; its twilight is a hundred years, and its twilight-portion is of like measure.

sanskrit: itareṣu sasaṃdhyeṣu sasaṃdhyāṃśeṣu ca triṣu ekāpāyena saṃyānti sahasrāṇi śatāni ca
english: In the other three ages, together with their twilights and twilight-portions, the thousands and the hundreds diminish, each by one unit.

sanskrit: etāni śāśvatāṃl lokān dhārayanti sanātanān etad brahmavidāṃ tāta viditaṃ brahma śāśvatam
english: These sustain the everlasting, eternal worlds; this, my son, is the eternal Brahman known to the knowers of Brahman.

sanskrit: catuṣpāt sakalo dharmaḥ satyaṃ caiva kṛte yuge nādharmeṇāgamaḥ kaś cit paras tasya pravartate
english: In the Kṛta age dharma stands whole on all four feet, and so does truth; no acquisition through unrighteousness ever arises to set against it.

sanskrit: itareṣv āgamād dharmaḥ pādaśas tv avaropyate caurikānṛtamāyābhir adharmaś copacīyate
english: In the other ages, through what is acquired, dharma is lowered foot by foot, and unrighteousness swells through theft, falsehood, and deceit.

sanskrit: arogāḥ sarvasiddhārthāś caturvarṣaśatāyuṣaḥ kṛte tretādiṣv eteṣāṃ pādaśo hrasate vayaḥ
english: In the Kṛta age men are free of disease, accomplished in all their aims, and live four hundred years; in the Tretā and the rest their span shortens foot by foot.

sanskrit: vedavādāś cānuyugaṃ hrasantīti ca naḥ śrutam āyūṃṣi cāśiṣaś caiva vedasyaiva ca yat phalam
english: And the teachings of the Veda diminish age by age—so we have heard—and so too do the life-spans, the benedictions, and the very fruit of the Veda.

sanskrit: anye kṛtayuge dharmās tretāyāṃ dvāpare 'pare anye kaliyuge dharmā yathāśaktikṛtā iva
english: The duties of the Kṛta age are one thing, those of the Tretā and the Dvāpara another, and those of the Kali age yet another—as though done according to one's capacity.

sanskrit: tapaḥ paraṃ kṛtayuge tretāyāṃ jñānam uttamam dvāpare yajñam evāhur dānam eva kalau yuge
english: In the Kṛta age austerity is supreme, in the Tretā knowledge is highest; in the Dvāpara they declare sacrifice foremost, and in the Kali age, giving alone.

sanskrit: etāṃ dvādaśasāhasrīṃ yugākhyāṃ kavayo viduḥ sahasraṃ parivṛttaṃ tad brāhmaṃ divasam ucyate
english: The wise know this cycle named the Yuga to span twelve thousand years; a thousand such cycles completed is called one Day of Brahmā.

sanskrit: rātris tāvat tithī brāhmī tadādau viśvam īśvaraḥ pralaye 'dhyātmam āviśya suptvā so 'nte vibudhyate
english: The Night of Brahmā is of equal length; at its beginning the Lord, at the dissolution, enters into the inner Self, and having slept, awakens at its end.

sanskrit: sahasrayugaparyantam ahar yad brahmaṇo viduḥ rātriṃ yugasahasrāntāṃ te 'horātravido janāḥ
english: Those who know the Day of Brahmā to extend through a thousand Yugas, and the Night to end with a thousand Yugas—those people know day and night truly.

sanskrit: pratibuddho vikurute brahmākṣayyaṃ kṣapākṣaye sṛjate ca mahad bhūtaṃ tasmād vyaktātmakaṃ manaḥ
english: Awakened at the passing of the night, Brahman transforms the imperishable and creates the Great Being, and from that the manifest-natured mind.

sanskrit: brahma tejomayaṃ śukraṃ yasya sarvam idaṃ jagat ekasya bhūtaṃ bhūtasya dvayaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamam
english: Brahman is luminous and radiant, of whom this whole world is born; from that single Being arose the twofold being, the moving and the unmoving.

sanskrit: ahar mukhe vibuddhaḥ san sṛjate vidyayā jagat agra eva mahābhūtam āśu vyaktātmakaṃ manaḥ
english: Awakened at the dawn of the Day, it creates the world by its knowledge, and foremost of all the Great Being, swiftly, the manifest-natured mind.

sanskrit: abhibhūyeha cārciṣmad vyasṛjat sapta mānasān dūragaṃ bahudhāgāmi prārthanāsaṃśayātmakam
english: Surpassing all and radiant, it emitted the seven mind-born ones—mind that ranges far, moves in many directions, and is the seat of desire and doubt.

sanskrit: manaḥ sṛṣṭiṃ vikurute codyamānaṃ sisṛkṣayā ākāśaṃ jāyate tasmāt tasya śabdo guṇo mataḥ
english: Mind, urged on by the will to create, brings forth creation; from it is born space, whose quality is held to be sound.

sanskrit: ākāśāt tu vikurvāṇāt sarvagandhavahaḥ śuciḥ balavāñ jāyate vāyus tasya sparśo guṇo mataḥ
english: From space as it transforms is born the wind, pure and mighty, the bearer of every scent, whose quality is held to be touch.

sanskrit: vāyor api vikurvāṇāj jyotir bhūtaṃ tamonudam rociṣṇu jāyate tatra tad rūpaguṇam ucyate
english: From the wind, too, as it transforms, is born the element of fire, dispeller of darkness and shining bright; its quality is said to be form.

sanskrit: jyotiṣo 'pi vikurvāṇād bhavanty āpo rasātmikāḥ adbhyo gandhaguṇā bhūmiḥ pūrvaiṣā sṛṣṭir ucyate
english: From fire too, as it transforms, arise the waters, whose essence is taste; from the waters comes earth, whose quality is scent—this is called the prior creation.

sanskrit: guṇāḥ pūrvasya pūrvasya prāpnuvanty uttarottaram teṣāṃ yāvat tithaṃ yad yat tat tat tāvad guṇaṃ smṛtam
english: The qualities of each preceding element pass on into each succeeding one; whatever the position each holds, that many qualities it is held to possess.

sanskrit: upalabhyāpsu ced gandhaṃ ke cid brūyur anaipuṇāt pṛthivyām eva taṃ vidyād āpo vāyuṃ ca saṃśritam
english: Should some, through want of discernment, claim to perceive scent in the waters, one should know that scent belongs to earth alone, residing also in water and in wind.

sanskrit: ete tu sapta puruṣā nānāviryāḥ pṛthak pṛthak nāśaknuvan prajāḥ sraṣṭum asamāgamya sarvataḥ
english: But these seven Puruṣas, of diverse powers, each apart, were unable to create the creatures so long as they had not joined together on every side.

sanskrit: te sametya mahātmānam anyonyam abhisaṃśritāḥ śarīrāśrayaṇaṃ prāptās tataḥ puruṣa ucyate
english: Coming together and resorting to one another, those great ones attained their lodging in a body; thence is the term Puruṣa, the embodied one, derived.

sanskrit: śrayaṇāc charīraṃ bhavati mūrtimat ṣoḍaśātmakam tad āviśanti bhūtāni mahānti saha karmaṇā
english: From their resorting together arises the body, embodied and made of sixteen constituents; the great elements enter into it together with action.

sanskrit: sarvabhūtāni cādāya tapasaś caraṇāya ca ādikartā mahābhūtaṃ tam evāhuḥ prajāpatim
english: Taking up all beings, for the practice of austerity, the primal Maker, the Great Being—him they call Prajāpati, the Lord of creatures.

sanskrit: sa vai sṛjati bhūtāni sa eva puruṣaḥ paraḥ ajo janayate brahmā devarṣipitṛmānavān
english: It is he who creates the beings; he alone is the supreme Puruṣa; unborn, as Brahmā he begets gods, sages, fathers, and men.

sanskrit: lokān nadīḥ samudrāṃś ca diśaḥ śailān vanaspatīn narakiṃnararakṣāṃsi vayaḥpaśumṛgoragān avyayaṃ ca vyayaṃ caiva dvayaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamam
english: He creates the worlds, the rivers and the oceans, the quarters, the mountains and the trees, men, kiṃnaras, and rākṣasas, birds, cattle, wild beasts, and serpents—both the imperishable and the perishable, the twofold realm of the unmoving and the moving.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ ye yāni karmāṇi prāk sṛṣṭyāṃ pratipedire tāny eva pratipadyante sṛjyamānāḥ punaḥ punaḥ
english: Whatever deeds these beings took up in the prior creation, those very deeds they take up again as they are created over and over.

sanskrit: hiṃsrāhiṃsre mṛdukrūre dharmādharme ṛtānṛte ato yan manyate dhātā tasmāt tat tasya rocate
english: Whether harmful or harmless, gentle or cruel, righteous or unrighteous, truthful or false—from this it follows that what the Ordainer assigns to each, that is what pleases him.

sanskrit: mahābhūteṣu nānātvam indriyārtheṣu mūrtiṣu viniyogaṃ ca bhūtānāṃ dhātaiva vidadhāty uta
english: The diversity among the great elements, in the objects of the senses and in embodied forms, and the appointment of beings to their tasks—it is the Ordainer alone who arranges all this.

sanskrit: ke cit puruṣakāraṃ tu prāhuḥ karmavido janāḥ daivam ity apare viprāḥ svabhāvaṃ bhūtacintakāḥ
english: Some, the men versed in action, declare human effort to be the cause; others, the brahmins, say it is destiny; and those who ponder the elements say it is inherent nature.

sanskrit: pauruṣaṃ karma daivaṃ ca phalavṛttisvabhāvataḥ traya ete 'pṛthagbhūtā navivekaṃ tu ke cana
english: Human exertion, action, and destiny—by the nature of how their fruits unfold, these three are not in truth distinct; yet some make no discernment of them at all.

sanskrit: evam etac ca naivaṃ ca yad bhūtaṃ sṛjate jagat karmasthā viṣamaṃ brūyuḥ sattvasthāḥ samadarśinaḥ
english: "It is thus, and yet it is not thus"—so men speak of the Being that creates the world; those wedded to action speak of inequality, while those grounded in goodness see with an equal eye.

sanskrit: tapo niḥśreyasaṃ jantos tasya mūlaṃ damaḥ śamaḥ tena sarvān avāpnoti yān kāmān manasecchati
english: Austerity is the highest good of a creature; its root is self-restraint and tranquillity; by it one attains all the desires the mind may wish.

sanskrit: tapasā tad avāpnoti yad bhūtaṃ sṛjate jagat sa tadbhūtaś ca sarveṣāṃ bhūtānāṃ bhavati prabhuḥ
english: By austerity one attains that Being which creates the world, and becoming one with that Being, he becomes the lord of all beings.

sanskrit: ṛṣayas tapasā vedān adhyaiṣanta divāniśam anādinidhanā nityā vāg utsṛṣṭā svayaṃbhuvā
english: By austerity the seers studied the Vedas day and night; speech, without beginning or end and eternal, was sent forth by the Self-existent.

sanskrit: ṛṣīṇāṃ nāmadheyāni yāś ca vedeṣu sṛṣṭayaḥ śarvaryanteṣu jātānāṃ tāny evaibhyo dadāti saḥ
english: The names of the seers, and the creations set forth in the Vedas—to those born at the ends of the nights he assigns those very same names and forms.

sanskrit: nāmabhedas tapaḥkarmayajñākhyā lokasiddhayaḥ ātmasiddhis tu vedeṣu procyate daśabhiḥ kramaiḥ
english: The distinctions of name, the designations of austerity, action, and sacrifice, are accomplishments of the world; but the realization of the Self is proclaimed in the Vedas through ten successive stages.

sanskrit: yad uktaṃ vedavādeṣu gahanaṃ vedadṛṣṭibhiḥ tadanteṣu yathāyuktaṃ kramayogena lakṣyate
english: What is set forth in the Vedic teachings, profound to those who see by the Vedas, is discerned, as is fitting, in the Vedānta through the practice of successive stages.

sanskrit: karmajo 'yaṃ pṛthagbhāvo dvaṃdvayukto viyoginaḥ ātmasiddhis tu vijñātā jahāti prāyaśo balam
english: This separateness born of action, bound to the pairs of opposites, belongs to one not yet released; but the realization of the Self, once understood, for the most part casts off its hold.

sanskrit: dve brahmaṇī veditavye śabdabrahma paraṃ ca yat śabdabrahmaṇi niṣṇātaḥ paraṃ brahmādhigacchati
english: Two Brahmans are to be known: the Brahman that is sound, and that which is supreme; one well-versed in the Brahman that is sound attains the supreme Brahman.

sanskrit: ārambhayajñāḥ kṣatrasya haviryajñā viśas tathā paricārayajñāḥ śūdrās tu tapoyajñā dvijātayaḥ
english: The sacrifice of undertakings belongs to the kṣatriya, the sacrifice of oblations to the vaiśya; service is the sacrifice of the śūdras, and austerity the sacrifice of the twice-born.

sanskrit: tretāyuge vidhis tv eṣāṃ yajñānāṃ na kṛte yuge dvāpare viplavaṃ yānti yajñāḥ kaliyuge tathā
english: The ordinance of these sacrifices belongs to the Tretā age, not to the Kṛta; in the Dvāpara the sacrifices fall into disorder, and so too in the Kali age.

sanskrit: apṛthagdharmiṇo martyā ṛksāmāni yajūṃṣi ca kāmyāṃ puṣṭiṃ pṛthag dṛṣṭvā tapobhis tapa eva ca
english: In the Kṛta age mortals were undivided in their duty; only on seeing the desired prosperity of the Ṛk, Sāma, and Yajus verses set apart did they practice austerity upon austerity.

sanskrit: tretāyāṃ tu samastās te prādurāsan mahābalāḥ saṃyantāraḥ sthāvarāṇāṃ jaṅgamānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ
english: But in the Tretā age all these appeared together, men of great might, restrainers of the unmoving and the moving on every side.

sanskrit: tretāyāṃ saṃhatā hy ete yajñā varṇās tathaiva ca saṃrodhād āyuṣas tv ete vyasyante dvāpare yuge
english: In the Tretā these sacrifices and the social orders alike held together; but through the shortening of the life-span they are dispersed in the Dvāpara age.

sanskrit: dṛśyante nāpi dṛśyante vedāḥ kaliyuge 'khilāḥ utsīdante sayajñāś ca kevalā dharmasetavaḥ
english: In the Kali age the Vedas are seen and yet not wholly seen; together with the sacrifices, the sole dikes of dharma fall away.

sanskrit: kṛte yuge yas tu dharmo brāhmaṇeṣu pradṛśyate ātmavatsu tapovatsu śrutavatsu pratiṣṭhitaḥ
english: The dharma that is seen among the brahmins in the Kṛta age stands firmly established in those who are self-possessed, austere, and learned in sacred lore.

sanskrit: adharmavratasaṃyogaṃ yathādharmaṃ yuge yuge vikriyante svadharmasthā vedavādā yathāyugam
english: Age by age, in keeping with the prevailing dharma, the teachings of the Veda, though grounded in their own law, are altered according to the age, taking on a contact with unrighteous observance.

sanskrit: yathā viśvāni bhūtāni vṛṣṭyā bhūyāṃsi prāvṛṣi sṛjyante jaṅgamasthāni tathā dharmā yuge yuge
english: Just as all moving beings are brought forth in greater abundance by rain in the season of the rains, so too are the dharmas in each successive age.

sanskrit: yathartuṣv ṛtuliṅgāni nānārūpāṇi paryaye dṛśyante tāni tāny eva tathā brahmāharātriṣu
english: As the marks of the seasons, in their many forms, are seen again and again, ever the same in their turning, so too are they seen in the Days and Nights of Brahmā.

sanskrit: vihitaṃ kālanānātvam anādinidhanaṃ tathā kīrtitaṃ yat purastāt te tat sūte cātti ca prajāḥ
english: The diversity of time, without beginning or end, is ordained; that which was proclaimed to you before brings forth the creatures and devours them again.

sanskrit: dadhāti prabhave sthānaṃ bhūtānāṃ saṃyamo yamaḥ svabhāvenaiva vartante dvaṃdvayuktāni bhūriśaḥ
english: Restraint, the curber, sets in place the station for the arising of beings; and abundantly the things bound to the pairs of opposites move on by their own inherent nature.

sanskrit: sargaḥ kālaḥ kriyā vedāḥ kartā kāryaṃ kriyā phalam proktaṃ te putra sarvaṃ vai yan māṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi
english: Creation, time, action, the Vedas, the doer, the deed to be done, action and its fruit—all this, my son, has been told to you, all that you have inquired of me.

sanskrit: pratyāhāraṃ tu vakṣyāmi śarvaryādau gate 'hani yathedaṃ kurute 'dhyātmaṃ susūkṣmaṃ viśvam īśvaraḥ
english: Now I shall speak of the withdrawal, when the Day is gone and the Night begins, how the Lord draws this universe into the most subtle inner Self.

sanskrit: divi sūryās tathā sapta dahanti śikhino 'rciṣā sarvam etat tadārcirbhiḥ pūrṇaṃ jājvalyate jagat
english: Then seven suns in the sky, flaming-crested, burn with their rays; and this whole world, filled with their flames, blazes forth ablaze.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca pṛthivyāṃ yāni bhūtāni jaṅgamāni dhruvāṇi ca tāny evāgre pralīyante bhūmitvam upayānti ca
english: Vyāsa said: Whatever beings there are upon the earth, moving and fixed, those first dissolve away and pass into the state of earth.

sanskrit: tataḥ pralīne sarvasmin sthāvare jaṅgame tathā akāṣṭhā nistṛṇā bhūmir dṛśyate kūrmapṛṣṭhavat
english: Then, when all has dissolved away, the unmoving and the moving alike, the earth, bare of wood and bare of grass, appears like the back of a tortoise.

sanskrit: bhūmer api guṇaṃ gandham āpa ādadate yadā āttagandhā tadā bhūmiḥ pralayatvāya kalpate
english: When the waters take up scent, the very quality of earth, then the earth, its scent taken from it, is made ready for dissolution.

sanskrit: āpas tataḥ pratiṣṭhanti ūrmimatyo mahāsvanāḥ sarvam evedam āpūrya tiṣṭhanti ca caranti ca
english: Then the waters stand established, billowing in waves and loud-roaring; filling all this, they stand and they flow.

sanskrit: apām api guṇāṃs tāta jyotir ādadate yadā āpas tadā āttaguṇā jyotiṣy uparamanti ca
english: When fire takes up the qualities of the waters too, my son, then the waters, their qualities taken away, come to rest within fire.

sanskrit: yadādityaṃ sthitaṃ madhye gūhanti śikhino 'rciṣaḥ sarvam evedam arcirbhiḥ pūrṇaṃ jājvalyate nabhaḥ
english: When the flaming rays conceal the sun set in the midst of heaven, then this whole sky, filled with flames, blazes forth ablaze.

sanskrit: jyotiṣo 'pi guṇaṃ rūpaṃ vāyur ādadate yadā praśāmyati tadā jyotir vāyur dodhūyate mahān
english: When the wind takes up form, the quality of fire too, then the fire is quenched, and the mighty wind blows tossing on every side.

sanskrit: tatas tu mūlam āsādya vāyuḥ saṃbhavam ātmanaḥ adhaś cordhvaṃ ca tiryak ca dodhavīti diśo daśa
english: Then, reaching the root, the source of its own being, the wind shakes violently below and above and sideways, through the ten directions.

sanskrit: vāyor api guṇaṃ sparśam ākāśaṃ grasate yadā praśāmyati tadā vāyuḥ khaṃ tu tiṣṭhati nānadat
english: When space swallows touch, the quality of wind too, then the wind is stilled, and space alone remains, resounding.

sanskrit: ākāśasya guṇaṃ śabdam abhivyaktātmakaṃ manaḥ manaso vyaktam avyaktaṃ brāhmaḥ sa pratisaṃcaraḥ
english: The manifest-natured mind takes up sound, the quality of space; from mind the manifest passes into the unmanifest—this is the reabsorption into Brahman.

sanskrit: tad ātmaguṇam āviśya mano grasati candramāḥ manasy uparate 'dhyātmā candramasy avatiṣṭhate
english: Entering that quality of the Self, the moon swallows the mind; and when the mind is stilled, the inner Self comes to rest within the moon.

sanskrit: taṃ tu kālena mahatā saṃkalpaḥ kurute vaśe cittaṃ grasati saṃkalpas tac ca jñānam anuttamam
english: After a great span of time, resolve brings that under its sway; resolve swallows the thinking faculty, and that supreme knowledge as well.

sanskrit: kālo girati vijñānaṃ kālo balam iti śrutiḥ balaṃ kālo grasati tu taṃ vidvān kurute vaśe
english: Time devours discernment—"Time is power," so runs the sacred teaching; Time swallows power, but the wise man brings even Time under his sway.

sanskrit: ākāśasya tadā ghoṣaṃ taṃ vidvān kurute ''tmani tad avyaktaṃ paraṃ brahma tac chāśvatam anuttamam evaṃ sarvāṇi bhūtāni brahmaiva pratisaṃcaraḥ
english: Then the wise man takes the sound of space into his own Self; that unmanifest is the supreme Brahman, eternal and unsurpassed—thus all beings are but Brahman, the reabsorption.

sanskrit: yathāvat kīrtitaṃ samyag evam etad asaṃśayam bodhyaṃ vidyāmayaṃ dṛṣṭvā yogibhiḥ paramātmabhiḥ
english: All this has been duly and rightly proclaimed, beyond doubt; it is to be understood, made of knowledge, beheld by yogins whose souls are set upon the supreme Self.

sanskrit: evaṃ vistārasaṃkṣepau brahmāvyakte punaḥ punaḥ yugasāhasrayor ādāv ahno rātryās tathaiva ca
english: Thus does the unmanifest Brahman expand and contract again and again, at the onset of the thousand Yugas of the Day and likewise of the Night.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca bhūtagrāme niyuktaṃ yat tad etat kīrtitaṃ mayā brāhmaṇasya tu yat kṛtyaṃ tat te vakṣyāmi pṛcchate
english: Vyāsa said: That which is appointed for the multitude of beings I have now proclaimed; but the duty proper to a brahmin I shall declare to you, since you ask.

sanskrit: jātakarmaprabhṛty asya karmaṇāṃ dakṣiṇāvatām kriyā syād ā samāvṛtter ācārye vedapārage
english: Beginning with the birth-rite, the performance of his sacraments, attended by their fees, should continue until his graduation, under a teacher who has mastered the Veda.

sanskrit: adhītya vedān akhilān guruśuśrūṣaṇe rataḥ gurūṇām anṛṇo bhūtvā samāvarteta yajñavit
english: Having studied all the Vedas, devoted to the service of his teacher, and become free of debt to his teachers, the knower of sacrifice should return home as a graduate.

sanskrit: ācāryeṇābhyanujñātaś caturṇām ekam āśramam ā vimokṣāc charīrasya so 'nutiṣṭhed yathāvidhi
english: With his teacher's leave, he should observe, according to rule, one of the four stations of life, until the release of the body.

sanskrit: prajāsargeṇa dāraiś ca brahmacaryeṇa vā punaḥ vane gurusakāśe vā yatidharmeṇa vā punaḥ
english: Whether by begetting offspring and taking a wife, or again by chastity, or in the forest in his teacher's presence, or again by the discipline of the ascetic.

sanskrit: gṛhasthas tv eva sarveṣāṃ caturṇāṃ mūlam ucyate tatra pakvakaṣāyo hi dāntaḥ sarvatra sidhyati
english: Yet the householder is called the root of all the four; for there the self-controlled man, whose impurities are ripened away, succeeds in every station.

sanskrit: prajāvāñ śrotriyo yajvā mukto divyais tribhir ṛṇaiḥ athānyān āśramān paścāt pūto gacchati karmabhiḥ
english: Blessed with offspring, learned in scripture, a performer of sacrifice, freed of the three divine debts—he then, purified by his deeds, may afterward pass on to the other stations of life.
